mainEntity.name: How soon after implant surgery is the first check-up usually scheduled?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timing of your first post-surgery implant check-up will depend on your individual treatment plan and clinical circumstances. It is commonly scheduled within the first one to two weeks following the procedure, allowing your dental team to assess the early stages of healing. Your dentist will advise you of your specific appointment schedule at the time of your surgery, and it is important to attend as recommended rather than waiting until you notice a problem.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to have some pain or discomfort before the first check-up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some degree of discomfort, mild swelling, and sensitivity in the days immediately following dental implant surgery can be a normal part of the healing process. This typically begins to improve within the first few days. If your symptoms are worsening rather than gradually subsiding, or if pain is not responding to any recommended pain relief, it is advisable to contact your dental practice for guidance before your scheduled appointment rather than waiting.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally before my post-surgery check-up appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should continue to follow the dietary guidance provided by your dental team in the post-operative period. This typically involves a soft diet that avoids placing excessive pressure on the implant site. Do not assume that it is safe to return to a normal diet simply because some time has passed since your surgery. Your dentist will advise you at the check-up appointment when and how to gradually reintroduce a wider range of foods safely.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a problem is identified at the check-up?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your dentist identifies any concerns during your first post-surgery check-up — such as signs of early infection, inadequate healing, or issues with the temporary restoration — they will discuss the findings with you clearly and explain what, if any, further action may be needed. This might involve additional monitoring, a change in oral hygiene guidance, or in some cases a further clinical intervention. All treatment decisions are made individually based on clinical assessment and your specific circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to stop any medications before my check-up appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, you do not need to stop any medications prior to a routine post-surgery check-up appointment. However, it is important to inform your dental team of any changes to your medications since your surgery, including any new prescriptions or over-the-counter medications you have started taking. If you have specific concerns about medications and your dental treatment, discuss these with both your dentist and your GP or prescribing clinician.

mainEntity.name: How long does the full dental implant process take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The duration of the dental implant process varies between patients and depends on a range of clinical factors, including bone density and volume, the location of the implant, and whether preparatory procedures such as bone grafting are required. Osseointegration alone typically takes several months. Your dental team will provide you with a treatment timeline tailored to your individual clinical situation during your consultation and treatment planning appointments.
